metadata.scope: Add tag master lifecycle operations to apps/api: (1) POST /admin/tags/:tagId/reactivate flips active=0 -> active=1 (idempotent no-op when already active; 404 tag_not_found when missing) with audit admin.tag.reactivated; (2) DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId/physical hard-deletes a tag_definitions row ONLY when no member_tags references exist, otherwise refuses with 409 tag_has_references (no orphan rows), with audit admin.tag.physically_deleted (before=full row, after=null). Extend tagDefinitions repository with reactivateTagDefinition, countMemberTagReferences, physicalDeleteTagDefinition; extend routes/admin/tags.ts audit action union and ERROR_TO_STATUS (tag_has_references: 409); add focused D1 Vitest specs; preserve the issue-1035 logical delete (DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId -> active=0) regression. No D1 schema migration is required (member_tags has no FK to tag_definitions, so the reference guard is application-level by design). No apps/web change. Physical delete is physical-deletion-2-stage: endpoint code + reference guard + audit + tests are implementable this cycle; only the production tag physical mutation runtime is user-gated via runbook. Issue #1070 stays CLOSED.

metadata.issue_optimization_note: Issue #1070 (= issue-1035 followup-003) frames reactivate + physical delete against the issue-1035 logical-delete contract. That contract is now landed (deactivateTagDefinition / DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId active=0 exist in current code). This spec is optimized to the CURRENT code: (1) reactivate and physical delete are confirmed NOT implemented anywhere (grep for reactivat / physical / 'DELETE FROM tag_definitions' across all branches = 0 hits) — the issue is unresolved and needs work. (2) AC-3 reference integrity: member_tags has NO database FOREIGN KEY to tag_definitions (PRIMARY KEY (member_id, tag_id) only, migrations/0002_admin_managed.sql:43), so physical delete CANNOT rely on ON DELETE cascade/restrict — the guard MUST be an application-level COUNT(*) on member_tags WHERE tag_id, and references>0 must return 409 tag_has_references without deleting (no orphan rows). (3) AC-1 separation: reactivate = POST /admin/tags/:tagId/reactivate (action sub-resource, distinct from PATCH label/category); physical delete = DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId/physical (distinct from logical DELETE /admin/tags/:tagId) so the issue-1035 logical-delete contract regression (AC-6) is preserved. (4) reactivate code-conflict (AC-2) is structurally impossible because reactivate flips active on the SAME row by tag_id and never touches the UNIQUE code column — documented as such rather than adding a spurious 409 path. (5) AuditAction is RepoBrand<string> (no enum) so admin.tag.reactivated / admin.tag.physically_deleted need no brand type change; AuditTargetType already includes 'tag'. The route's appendTagAudit action union ('admin.tag.created'|'updated'|'deactivated') is the only type literal that must be extended. (6) Physical delete frees the UNIQUE code (row gone) whereas logical delete keeps it occupied (active=0 row remains) — this distinction is the operational reason both lifecycle ops are needed.
